claim: ART has transformed HIV-1 from a fatal disease to a chronic condition
source: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) has transformed human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) from a fatal disease to a chronic condition.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in HIV medicine supported by decades of clinical evidence

claim: ART must be taken life-long as interruption of therapy in PLWH mostly results in viral rebound within weeks
source: However, ART must be taken life-long as interruption of therapy in people living with HIV-1 (PLWH) mostly results in viral rebound within weeks (Davey et al., 1999; Crowell et al., 2019; Bar et al., 2016; Buzon et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: Viral rebound results from cells harboring HIV-1 DNA that is integrated into the host genome
source: This rebound results from cells harboring HIV-1 DNA that is integrated into the host genome.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HIV reservoir biology

claim: More than 95% of proviral DNA is replication-incompetent
source: While >95% of proviral DNA is replication-incompetent, the remaining fraction that we define here as the 'HIV-1 reservoir', retains the capacity to produce infectious virus particles
evidence: This is a well-established finding in HIV reservoir research

claim: The HIV-1 reservoir is present in blood cells at a low frequency of approximately 1 in 10^6 resting CD4+ T cells
source: The inducible form of the HIV-1 reservoir is present in blood cells at a low frequency (~1 in 106 resting CD4+ T cells)
evidence: This is a well-documented characteristic of the HIV reservoir

claim: The HIV-1 reservoir has an estimated half-life of 44 months
source: The inducible form of the HIV-1 reservoir is present in blood cells at a low frequency (~1 in 106 resting CD4+ T cells), but is highly stable, with an estimated half-life of 44 months (Crooks et al., 2015; Siliciano and Siliciano, 2015; Siliciano and Siliciano, 2004).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: Natural decay of the HIV-1 reservoir would take more than 70 years
source: Natural decay of the HIV-1 reservoir would therefore take >70 years (Crooks et al., 2015; Siliciano and Siliciano, 2015; Siliciano and Siliciano, 2004).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: CD8+ T cells can produce cytokines or release lytic molecules killing infected cells upon peptide recognition
source: On peptide recognition, CD8+ T cells can produce cytokines or release lytic molecules killing the infected cell.
evidence: This is established immunological knowledge about CD8+ T cell function

claim: CD8+ T cells contribute to the control of untreated HIV-1
source: There is significant evidence that CD8+ T cells contribute to the control of untreated HIV-1, supported by studies of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) in non-human primates (Pandrea et al., 2011; Barouch et al., 2002; Schmitz et al., 2005; McBrien et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: HLA-I types B*57:01/:03 and B*27:05 are overrepresented in HIV-1 elite virus controllers
source: First, certain HLA-I types, such as B*57:01/:03 and B*27:05, are overrepresented in HIV-1 elite virus controllers, defined as PLWH who exhibit sustained HIV-1 control below 50 copies/ml without ART.
evidence: This is a well-established finding in HIV immunology research

claim: HIV-1-specific CD8+ T cells exert significant immune pressure on HIV-1, resulting in the accumulation of non-synonymous mutations in and around reactive T cell epitopes
source: Second, HIV-1-specific CD8+ T cells exert significant immune pressure on HIV-1, resulting in the accumulation of non-synonymous mutations in and around reactive T cell epitopes that can confer escape from CD8+ T cell recognition and killing (Borrow et al., 1997; Goulder et al., 1997; Phillips et al., 1991; Price et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: HIV-1 escape from CD8+ T cells is typically measured as a ≥ 50% decrease in the magnitude of the T cell response
source: HIV-1 escape from CD8+ T cells, which is typically measured as a ≥ 50% decrease in the magnitude of the T cell response, can occur within days to weeks of infection (Borrow et al., 1997; Price et al., 1997; Koup et al., 1994; Goonetilleke et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: T cell immunodominance and viral entropy are major determinants of the rate of virus escape in untreated infection
source: Both T cell immunodominance (relative strength of a T cell response) and viral entropy (sequence conservation of HIV-1 at a population level) are major determinants of the rate of virus escape in untreated infection (Liu et al., 2013; Ferrari et al., 2011; Barton et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: Virus escape is ongoing in untreated HIV-1 infection
source: Notably, virus escape is ongoing in untreated HIV-1 infection (Allen et al., 2005), with new virus variants emerging over time in response to newly induced T cell responses, shifts in T cell clonotypes, or to compensate for fitness costs of earlier mutations.
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: When T cell selection pressure is removed, reversion of mutations can occur
source: Lastly, when T cell selection pressure is removed, as in the case of virus transmission to recipients with HLA alleles different from the donor, reversion of mutations can occur (Leslie et al., 2004; Carlson et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: ART is highly effective in inhibiting viral replication
source: ART is highly effective in inhibiting viral replication with multiple studies reporting that HIV-1 does not undergo directional selection during suppressive ART (Kearney et al., 2014; Kearney et al., 2016; Rosenbloom et al., 2017; Van Zyl et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: The majority of proviruses that persist during ART reflect viruses circulating during the year prior to ART initiation
source: Recent studies have reported that the majority of proviruses, both total HIV-1 DNA and replication-competent viruses, that persist during ART, reflect viruses circulating during the year prior to ART initiation (Brodin et al., 2016; Abrahams et al., 2019; Pankau et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: ART initiation is the major driver of latency formation, including the formation of the replication-competent stable HIV-1 reservoir
source: These studies suggest that ART initiation is the major driver of latency formation, including the formation of the replication-competent stable HIV-1 reservoir.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited studies

claim: Proviruses that persist during ART include HIV-1 variants that have escaped from T cell selection over the entire course of untreated infection
source: Proviruses that persist during ART would therefore include HIV-1 variants that have escaped from T cell selection over the entire course of untreated infection (Phillips et al., 1991; Deng et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citations to published studies

claim: ART impacts the HIV-1-specific T cell response, with reduced HIV-1 loads resulting in lower antigen drive and over time, yielding improved proliferation and a less exhausted T cell phenotype
source: ART also impacts the HIV-1-specific T cell response, with reduced HIV-1 loads resulting in lower antigen drive and over time, yielding improved proliferation and a less exhausted T cell phenotype (Rehr et al., 2008; Rutishauser et al., 2017) (reviewed in Warren et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: HIV-1-specific T cell responses are detectable ex vivo and are highly stable in PLWH on durable ART suppression
source: We have recently shown that HIV-1-specific T cell responses are detectable ex vivo and are highly stable in PLWH on durable ART suppression (Xu et al., 2019)
evidence: Supported by citation to published study by the authors

claim: Ex vivo isolated CD8+ T cells can suppress HIV-1 superinfected CD4+ T cells as well as in vitro reactivated reservoir virus
source: with others showing that ex vivo isolated CD8+ T cells can suppress HIV-1 superinfected CD4+ T cells as well as in vitro reactivated reservoir virus (Sung et al., 2015; Shan et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Up to 98% of proviral HIV-1 sequences harbored mutations in immunoprevalent viral epitopes
source: Of note, a recent study reported that up to 98% of proviral HIV-1 sequences harbored mutations in immunoprevalent viral epitopes, though unmutated targets were also identified (Deng et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: The study cohort consisted of 25 PLWH durably suppressed by combination ART with viral load <50 copies/ml for 1.6–20.1 years (mean 7.2 years)
source: HIV-1-specific T cell responses and the size of the HIV-1 reservoir were measured in 25 PLWH (ages 25–66, mean 46; male = 16, female = 9) durably suppressed by combination ART (viral load <50 copies/ml for 1.6–20.1 years, mean 7.2 years).
evidence: This is data from the study cohort

claim: Four participants initiated ART during acute HIV-1 infection, while 21 initiated ART during chronic HIV-1 infection
source: Of the 25 participants, four initiated ART during acute HIV-1 infection, while the other 21 initiated ART during chronic HIV-1 infection (see Materials and Methods for definitions).
evidence: This is data from the study cohort

claim: OGV sequences from different timepoints for each participant were interspersed within-host phylogenetic trees, suggesting no major directional selection over time while participants remained suppressed on ART
source: OGV sequences from different timepoints for each participant were interspersed within-host phylogenetic trees, suggesting no major directional selection over time while participants remained suppressed on ART (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from phylogenetic analysis of longitudinal data shown in figures

claim: Participants were infected with HIV-1 clade B, except for one participant who was infected with HIV-1 clade G
source: Participants were infected with HIV-1 clade B, except for one participant (participant 00926) who was infected with HIV-1 clade G.
evidence: This is data from phylogenetic analysis

claim: Participants treated during acute infection showed greater genetic similarity than sequences from participants treated during chronic infection
source: Available HIV-1 sequences from participants treated during acute infection (n = 3) showed greater genetic similarity (maximum pairwise diversity 0.0007) than sequences from participants treated during chronic infection (n = 19) (maximum pairwise diversity 0.0088) (Mann-Whitney two tailed test, p=0.003, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is data from phylogenetic analysis with statistical testing

claim: Most HIV-1 infections are established from a single HIV-1 variant
source: This is consistent with reports in which most HIV-1 infections are established from a single HIV-1 variant, and therefore the early onset of ART, which halts viral evolution, results in a smaller and more homogenous HIV-1 reservoir (Kearney et al., 2014; Keele et al., 2008; Haaland et al., 2009; Derdeyn et al., 2004; Abrahams et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: The proportion of HLA-associated sites exhibiting the HLA-adapted form ranged from 9–33% within participants
source: Within participants, the proportion of HLA-associated sites exhibiting the HLA-adapted form ranged from 9–33% (adapted) and 32–66% (adapted + possibly adapted), and varied markedly by HIV-1 protein (Carlson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is data from bioinformatics analysis of HLA-associated polymorphisms

claim: Between 52 and 80% of HLA-associated sites in the HIV-1 reservoir were predicted to retain susceptibility to host HLA-restricted T cell responses
source: Importantly, our observation that, across all HIV-1 proteins, the minimum and maximum bounds for within-host escape burden ranged from 20% (adapted only) to 48% (adapted + possibly adapted) meant that between 52 and 80% of HLA-associated sites in the HIV-1 reservoir were predicted to retain susceptibility to host HLA-restricted T cell responses.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the bioinformatics analysis data

claim: A total of 166 reactive T cell epitopes were identified across the 25 participants
source: Across the 25 participants, a total of 166 reactive T cell epitopes were identified (see Methods for positivity criteria).
evidence: This is data from T cell mapping experiments

claim: The mean summed magnitude of HIV-1-specific T cell responses was 1,033 SFU/M (range: 156–2,856 SFU/M)
source: The mean summed magnitude of HIV-1-specific T cell responses was 1,033 SFU/M (range: 156–2,856 SFU/M), and the mean T cell breadth was seven reactive epitopes (range: 1–19 epitopes) per participant (Table 2).
evidence: This is data from T cell mapping experiments

claim: The mean T cell breadth was seven reactive epitopes per participant (range: 1–19 epitopes)
source: The mean summed magnitude of HIV-1-specific T cell responses was 1,033 SFU/M (range: 156–2,856 SFU/M), and the mean T cell breadth was seven reactive epitopes (range: 1–19 epitopes) per participant (Table 2).
evidence: This is data from T cell mapping experiments

claim: The magnitude of the mean summed HIV-1-specific T cell response correlated positively with the breadth of reactive epitopes targeted
source: Predictably, and consistent with reports in untreated HIV-1 infection, the magnitude of the mean summed HIV-1-specific T cell response correlated positively with the breadth of reactive epitopes targeted (r = 0.57, Spearman Rank two-tailed, p=0.003, 25 pairs, Supplementary file 7; Addo et al., 2003).
evidence: This is data from statistical analysis of T cell mapping experiments

claim: The highest magnitude T cell response within a participant most frequently targeted Gag and Nef
source: For example, the highest magnitude T cell response within a participant (immunodominant T cell response) most frequently targeted Gag and Nef, whereas the most frequently targeted protein across the cohort (immunoprevalent T cell response) was Gag (Figure 4—figure supplement 1; Addo et al., 2003).
evidence: This is data from T cell mapping experiments shown in figure

claim: No differences in either T cell magnitude or breadth were observed between women and men
source: No differences in either T cell magnitude or breadth were observed between women and men, or between participants treated during acute versus chronic HIV-1 infection (Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This is data from statistical analysis of T cell mapping experiments

claim: No differences in either T cell magnitude or breadth were observed between participants treated during acute versus chronic HIV-1 infection
source: No differences in either T cell magnitude or breadth were observed between women and men, or between participants treated during acute versus chronic HIV-1 infection (Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This is data from statistical analysis of T cell mapping experiments

claim: Neither T cell magnitude nor breadth exhibited any association with measured HIV-1 IUPM
source: Neither T cell magnitude nor breadth exhibited any association with measured HIV-1 IUPM (Supplementary file 8; Xu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is data from statistical analysis

claim: The majority (68%) of T cell epitopes harbored no detectable escape mutations
source: The majority (68%) of T cell epitopes harbored no detectable escape mutations.
evidence: This is a key finding from the empirical escape testing experiments

claim: Virus escape was confirmed in 49 of 151 (32%) HIV-1 T cell epitopes
source: In total, virus escape was confirmed in the replication-competent HIV-1 reservoir in 49 of 151 (32%) HIV-1 T cell epitopes (Figure 4D)
evidence: This is data from empirical escape testing experiments shown in figure

claim: In each participant, one third (average = 34%) of reactive epitopes harbored virus escape mutations
source: In each participant, one third (average = 34%) of reactive epitopes harbored virus escape mutations (Figure 4E, Table 2).
evidence: This is data from empirical escape testing experiments shown in figure and table

claim: In six participants, no T cell escape was observed in any reactive T cell epitope
source: In six participants, no T cell escape was observed in any reactive T cell epitope (i.e. 0% escape in 3–7 epitopes, additional DNA sequencing in Figure 4—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is data from empirical escape testing experiments shown in figure

claim: On average for each epitope, 27% of OGV sequences tested produced a ≥ 50% loss in T cell response
source: On average for each epitope, 27% of OGV sequences tested produced a ≥ 50% loss in T cell response (Figure 4F, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is data from empirical escape testing experiments shown in figure

claim: No differences in the depth of virus escape was observed between participants treated in acute or chronic infection
source: No differences in the depth of virus escape was observed between participants treated in acute or chronic infection (Figure 4F, Mann-Whitney two-tailed test, p=0.216).
evidence: This is data from statistical analysis of escape testing experiments shown in figure

claim: Escape was more commonly observed in regions of higher Shannon entropy
source: As expected, escape was more commonly observed in regions of higher Shannon entropy (Mann-Whitney two-tailed test, p=0.009) (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is data from statistical analysis shown in figure

claim: Immunodominance of circulating T cell responses in PLWH on ART did not associate with the presence or absence of escape within the cognate epitope
source: While our previous work in untreated HIV-1 infection reported that immunodominance is a major determinant in the time to viral escape, immunodominance of circulating T cell responses in PLWH on ART did not associate with the presence or absence of escape within the cognate epitope (Mann-Whitney two-tailed test, p=0.971, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is data from statistical analysis shown in figure

claim: The HIVconsX immunogen contained 59/151 (39%) of circulating T cell responses observed in the dataset
source: The HIVconsX immunogen contained the largest number of circulating T cell responses observed in our dataset (59/151; 39%; mean of 3 epitopes/participant, range 0–6)
evidence: This is data from analysis of vaccine immunogen coverage

claim: Escape frequency was on average twofold lower in reactive T cell epitopes found within the immunogens relative to those excluded from immunogen designs
source: Nevertheless, escape frequency was on average twofold lower in reactive T cell epitopes (12–29%) found within the immunogens relative to those excluded from immunogen designs (33–44%).
evidence: This is data from analysis of vaccine immunogen coverage and escape

claim: The proportion of reactive T cell epitopes within the HIVconsX immunogen that contained escape variants was 15.3% (9/59 epitopes)
source: For example, the overall proportion of reactive T cell epitopes within the HIVconsX immunogen that contained escape variants was 15.3% (9/59 epitopes, average 0 escape epitopes/participant, range 0–2)
evidence: This is data from analysis of vaccine immunogen coverage and escape

claim: The proportion of reactive T cell epitopes outside of the HIVconsX immunogen that contained escape variants was 43.5%
source: whereas the proportion of reactive T cell epitopes outside of the HIVconsX immunogen that contained escape variants was almost >2.5-fold higher (43.5%, average two escape epitopes/participant).
evidence: This is data from analysis of vaccine immunogen coverage and escape

claim: The difference in escape frequency between epitopes within and outside the HIVconsX immunogen was statistically significant (p=0.001)
source: This difference was statistically significant (p=0.001, Pearson's χ2 test with Yates correction, Supplementary file 9).
evidence: This is data from statistical analysis

claim: 20% of HLA-associated sites in the HIV-1 reservoir harbored the known HLA-adapted viral form
source: Overall, 20% of HLA-associated sites in the HIV-1 reservoir harbored the known HLA-adapted viral form, suggesting potential viral escape from T cell responses.
evidence: This is data from bioinformatics analysis of HLA-associated polymorphisms

claim: 48% of HLA-associated sites harbored known or putative HLA-adapted forms
source: This number increased to 48% if both known and putative HLA-adapted forms were included in the calculation.
evidence: This is data from bioinformatics analysis of HLA-associated polymorphisms

claim: The minimal empirically defined T cell escape frequency of 32% observed in PLWH on ART is consistent with studies of T cell escape in untreated HIV-1 infection
source: The minimal empirically defined T cell escape frequency of 32% observed in PLWH on ART in this study is consistent with studies of T cell escape in untreated HIV-1 infection.
evidence: This is a comparison of the study findings with published literature

claim: A 30% escape frequency was observed in primary untreated HIV-1 infection
source: A 30% escape frequency was observed in primary untreated HIV-1 infection, in which HIV-1-specific T cell responses were comprehensively mapped against the autologous transmitted/founder virus in participants, and T cell reactivity was assessed against mutant viruses that emerged over the first 6 months of infection (Liu et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: A similar escape frequency of 33% was observed in a large cross-sectional study of chronically infected HIV-1 Clade C untreated individuals
source: A similar escape frequency of 33% was also observed in a large cross-sectional study of chronically infected HIV-1 Clade C untreated individuals (n >2,000), in which the T cell escape frequency was determined by examining participant HLA-associated polymorphisms in immunoprevalent HIV-1 CD8+ T cell epitopes (Carlson et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: HIV-1-specific T cell responses are stable and maintain immunodominance hierarchies over years in PLWH durably suppressed on ART
source: In PLWH durably suppressed on ART, HIV-1-specific T cell responses are stable and maintain immunodominance hierarchies over years (Xu et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: The HIV-1 reservoir is mostly formed at the time of ART initiation
source: These studies showed that the HIV-1 reservoir is mostly formed at the time of ART initiation (Brodin et al., 2016; Abrahams et al., 2019; Pankau et al., 2020)
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: The rate of decay of the HIV-1 reservoir is very slow
source: and its subsequent rate of decay is very slow (Crooks et al., 2015; Siliciano and Siliciano, 2015; Siliciano and Siliciano, 2004)
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: Longitudinal analyses of near full-length proviral sequences in PLWH on ART showed no enrichment in escaped epitopes over time
source: More recently, longitudinal analyses of near full-length proviral sequences in PLWH on ART showed no enrichment in escaped epitopes over time suggesting that HIV-1-specific T cells do not significantly alter the provirus landscape in people durably suppressed (Antar et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: Brief analytical treatment interruption does not significantly impact the composition of virus populations or size of the latent HIV-1 reservoir
source: Furthermore, a recent study reported that brief analytical treatment interruption (ATI) (median of 5 weeks) does not significantly impact the composition of virus populations (phylogenetic analyses sequencing of HIV-1 env) or size (total DNA, cell-associated RNA, IUPM) of the latent HIV-1 reservoir (Salantes et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: Circulating T cells and virus escape variants in infected cells at the time of ART initiation are maintained throughout durable viral suppression
source: Collectively, these studies suggest a model in which circulating T cells, as well as virus escape variants in infected cells at the time of ART initiation, are maintained throughout durable viral suppression, and during brief periods of ATI.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from multiple cited studies

claim: Deng et al. reported a predominance of CD8+ T cell-resistant viruses in proviral HIV-1 DNA
source: Our observations contrast somewhat with those of Deng and colleagues who reported a predominance of CD8+ T cell-resistant viruses in proviral HIV-1 DNA (Deng et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: T cell escape is rarely all-or-nothing, but rather occurs at different rates with multiple variants emerging over time
source: Our observations that epitopes mostly harbor a mix of escape and non-escape variants are consistent with previous studies in untreated infection reporting that T cell escape is rarely all-or-nothing, but rather occurs at different rates (days to years) with multiple variants emerging over time (Goonetilleke et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2013; Asquith et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: Almost 30% of sequences enter the HIV-1 reservoir much earlier than ART initiation
source: While the HIV-1 reservoir is mostly formed at ART initiation, almost 30% of sequences enter the HIV-1 reservoir much earlier.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HIV reservoir formation

claim: The average depth of sequencing (25 sequences/participant) provided 95% confidence that any undetected variant comprised <12% of the population
source: Applying a rule of three calculation, our average depth of sequencing (25 sequences/participant) provided 95% confidence that any undetected variant comprised <12% of the population.
evidence: This is a statistical calculation based on the sequencing data

claim: Recombinant viruses rapidly emerge following HIV rebound
source: Recent work has shown recombinant viruses rapidly emerge following HIV rebound (Vibholm et al., 2019; Lu et al., 2018; Cohen et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: Circulating HIV-1-specific T cells very likely afford some contribution in control of virus rebound
source: Our study, supported by animal models (Pandrea et al., 2011) and case reports investigating viral rebound (Smith et al., 2015), suggest that circulating HIV-1-specific T cells very likely afford some contribution in control of virus rebound.
evidence: This is an inference supported by citations to published studies

claim: T cell immunity is rapidly overwhelmed, in part due to recombination-mediated escape
source: However, T cell immunity is rapidly overwhelmed, in part due to recombination-mediated escape (Ritchie et al., 2014; Streeck et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: HIV-1 cure strategies that include efforts to augment T cell immunity in PLWH on ART should include immunogen designs that target existing T cell epitopes, particularly those with low entropy
source: Altogether, this suggests that HIV-1 cure strategies that include efforts to augment T cell immunity in PLWH on ART should include immunogen designs that target existing T cell epitopes, particularly those with low entropy which, as we show here, are less likely to harbor escape in the replication-competent reservoir.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the study findings

claim: Success of HIV-1 cure therapies will likely be dependent on the ability to exert very rapid virus control and to limit the emergence of viral recombinants
source: Ultimately, success of these therapies will likely be dependent on the ability to exert very rapid virus control and to limit the emergence of viral recombinants.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future therapeutic approaches

claim: Within the cohort, IUPM measurements ranged from below the limit of detection to 2.528 IUPM
source: Within the cohort, measurements ranged from below the limit of detection (participants 00941 and 20296, see Material and Methods for definition of limit of detection) to 2.528 IUPM (Table 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is data from QVOA measurements

claim: PacBio sequencing provided long reads which identified sites of virus diversity within and outside epitopes
source: PacBio sequencing provided long reads (two reactions spanned almost the entire length of HIV-1) which identified sites of virus diversity within and outside epitopes that were reactive in initial T cell mapping (see Materials and Methods describing 'stripes').
evidence: This describes the technical approach used in the study

claim: Only 4–5 mutations are expected across the virus genome over the 15 day QVOA culture
source: Note that given the initial effective population size in each well was, on average, n = 1 (Rouzine et al., 2001), in vitro mutations occurred stochastically, with only 4–5 mutations expected across the virus genome over the 15 day QVOA culture (Song et al., 2012; Brown and Richman, 1997).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Phylogenetic analysis confirmed that sequences from each participant formed monophyletic clades
source: Phylogenetic analysis of the 22 participants for whom near full-length sequencing was available (mean = 16 sequences per participant, range 1–71) confirmed that sequences from each participant formed monophyletic clades (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is data from phylogenetic analysis shown in figures

claim: The 5' and 3' half genome sequences from two participants exhibited >20% clonality
source: In general, identical OGV sequences (see definition in Materials and Methods) were identified only infrequently; however, the 5' and 3' half genome sequences from two participants (participants 00250 and 00749, Figure 3A and E) exhibited >20% clonality, consistent with reports that in that the HIV-1 reservoir is in part maintained by clonal expansion (Supplementary file 3; Bui et al., 2017).
evidence: This is data from sequencing analysis shown in figures, supported by citation

claim: The magnitude of the HIV-1-specific T cell response was weaker compared to untreated HIV-1 infection
source: As noted above, while the magnitude of the HIV-1-specific T cell response was weaker compared to untreated HIV-1 infection, the pattern of HIV-1 proteins targeted by T cells was similar to previous reports of untreated infection (Figure 4B; Xu et al., 2019; Addo et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a comparison with published literature, supported by citations

claim: The pattern of HIV-1 proteins targeted by T cells was similar to previous reports of untreated infection
source: As noted above, while the magnitude of the HIV-1-specific T cell response was weaker compared to untreated HIV-1 infection, the pattern of HIV-1 proteins targeted by T cells was similar to previous reports of untreated infection (Figure 4B; Xu et al., 2019; Addo et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a comparison with published literature, supported by citations

claim: Escape occurred more frequently in epitopes in Pol, Env and Nef proteins
source: In total, virus escape was confirmed in the replication-competent HIV-1 reservoir in 49 of 151 (32%) HIV-1 T cell epitopes (Figure 4D) with escape occurring more frequently in epitopes in Pol, Env and Nef (25%, 23%, 21%) proteins (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is data from empirical escape testing experiments shown in figure

claim: In the two participants who responded to only one epitope, virus escape was confirmed in both cases
source: In six participants, no T cell escape was observed in any reactive T cell epitope (i.e. 0% escape in 3–7 epitopes, additional DNA sequencing in Figure 4—figure supplement 2), whereas in the two participants who responded to only one epitope, virus escape was confirmed in both cases (i.e. 100% escape) (Figure 4E, Table 2).
evidence: This is data from empirical escape testing experiments shown in figure and table

claim: The range of within-epitope escape was broad, starting at 1–2% to 100% of all OGVs
source: The range of within-epitope escape was broad, starting at 1–2% to 100% of all OGVs.
evidence: This is data from empirical escape testing experiments

claim: An escape depth of 100% occurred when all OGVs were identical but induced a lower T cell response than the originally tested consensus clade B epitope
source: Note, that an escape depth of 100% (which was observed for n = 5 epitopes) occurred when all OGVs were identical but induced a lower T cell response than the originally tested consensus clade B epitope.
evidence: This is an explanation of the data from empirical escape testing experiments

claim: Multiple well-characterized immunoprevalent epitopes harbored a mix of escape and non-escape OGVs, but overall, mostly non-escape
source: Our mapping included multiple, well-characterized immunoprevalent epitopes that also harbored a mix of escape and non-escape OGVs, but overall, mostly non-escape (Figure 4F, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is data from empirical escape testing experiments shown in figure

claim: Current conserved immunogen designs are likely to be immunogenic in PLWH on ART
source: This suggests that current conserved immunogen designs are likely to be immunogenic in PLWH on ART and are more likely to target T cell epitopes that do not harbor pre-ART escape.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the vaccine immunogen analysis data

claim: Current conserved immunogen designs are more likely to target T cell epitopes that do not harbor pre-ART escape
source: This suggests that current conserved immunogen designs are likely to be immunogenic in PLWH on ART and are more likely to target T cell epitopes that do not harbor pre-ART escape.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the vaccine immunogen analysis data

claim: The p24 CE vaccine contained the least number of circulating T cell responses (16/151; 11%)
source: The HIVconsX immunogen contained the largest number of circulating T cell responses observed in our dataset (59/151; 39%; mean of 3 epitopes/participant, range 0–6) while the p24 CE vaccine contained the least (16/151; 11%; mean of 1 epitope/participant, range 0–4) (Figure 4H, Supplementary file 9).
evidence: This is data from analysis of vaccine immunogen coverage shown in figure

claim: The other three conserved immunogen vaccines also targeted T cell epitopes with a low rate of escape
source: Similarly, the other three conserved immunogen vaccines also targeted T cell epitopes with a low rate of escape (Létourneau et al., 2007; Mothe et al., 2015a; Kulkarni et al., 2013).
evidence: This is data from analysis of vaccine immunogen coverage, supported by citations

claim: The majority of circulating HIV-specific T cell responses were able to fully recognize the autologous replication-competent-reservoir virus
source: We then systematically examined whether non-synonymous mutations in reactive epitopes impacted T cell recognition and functional responses. Consistent with the overall HLA-adaptation estimates from the bioinformatics analysis, we experimentally confirmed that 32% (49/151) of all reactive T cell epitopes in HIV-1 OGVs contained mutations that conferred T cell escape, and that conversely, 68% of circulating HIV-specific T cell responses were able to fully recognize the autologous replication-competent-reservoir virus.
evidence: This is a key finding from the empirical escape testing experiments
